cases.prompt: Investigate and fix an authentication bug without changing the existing authenticate(header, expectedToken) API. User report: `Bearer secret-extra` is accepted when expectedToken is `secret`; missing or empty configured tokens must never authenticate. Inspect the cause and obtain an independent security assessment of credential parsing, fail-closed configuration and residual exposure before the fix; the assessment is required because callers rely on this credential boundary. Keep valid exact Bearer authentication working and add negative regressions. Reject non-string/missing header, wrong scheme, empty token and extra suffixes. This disposable fixture is not a production authentication system. Do not introduce a new identity architecture, install dependencies, log secrets, or access external services.

files.auth.js: export function authenticate(header, expectedToken) { return typeof header==='string' && header.startsWith('Bearer '+expectedToken); }
files.auth.test.js: import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {authenticate} from './auth.js';test('valid token',()=>assert.equal(authenticate('Bearer secret','secret'),true));

cases.prompt: Refactor the duplicated invoice amount formatting into an internal formatCents(cents) helper in money.js and reuse it from receipt.js. Preserve the receipt(id,cents) exported API and every existing output byte, including negative amounts and zero. This is internal restructuring, not a new API boundary or currency design. Add focused behavior-preservation coverage and run the existing tests. Work only in this disposable personal fixture; no dependencies.

files.receipt.js:
export function receipt(id,cents){const sign=cents<0?'-':'';const abs=Math.abs(cents);return id+': '+sign+Math.floor(abs/100)+'.'+String(abs%100).padStart(2,'0');}
export function refund(cents){const sign=cents<0?'-':'';const abs=Math.abs(cents);return 'refund '+sign+Math.floor(abs/100)+'.'+String(abs%100).padStart(2,'0');}
files.receipt.test.js: import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {receipt,refund} from './receipt.js';test('receipt output',()=>{assert.equal(receipt('a',123),'a: 1.23');assert.equal(refund(-12),'refund -0.12');});

cases.prompt: Review retry.js for correctness of failure propagation and retry limits, including an independent read-only review of the scoped source. The intended contract is at most attempts calls, return the first success, reject with the final original error if every call fails, and reject invalid attempt counts before calling fn. Independently check and evaluate the findings rather than returning an uninspected verdict. Give evidence-backed findings, severity and focused checks. This is review only: do not modify any files and do not run tests. The fixture is disposable; no install or external access.

files.retry.js: export async function retry(fn,attempts=3){for(let i=0;i<attempts;i++){try{return await fn();}catch{}}}
files.retry.test.js: import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {retry} from './retry.js';test('retries a transient failure',async()=>{let n=0;assert.equal(await retry(()=>{if(++n===1)throw Error('transient');return 7;}),7);assert.equal(n,2);});

files.benchmark.test.js: import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {performance} from 'node:perf_hooks';import {resolve} from './catalog.js';test('fixed lookup workload',()=>{const records=Array.from({length:20000},(_,id)=>({id,value:id*2}));const ids=Array.from({length:12000},(_,i)=>(i*37)%22000);resolve(records,ids.slice(0,500));const times=[];for(let n=0;n<3;n++){const start=performance.now();const result=resolve(records,ids);times.push(performance.now()-start);assert.equal(result[1].value,74);assert.equal(result.length,12000);}times.sort((a,b)=>a-b);console.log('MEASURE '+times[1].toFixed(3)+' ms median fixed-20000x12000 repeats=3');});

cases.prompt: Make the existing SQLite users migration atomic and provide rollback(db), preserving the migrate(db) API. Version 0 has users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,name TEXT NOT NULL). Version 1 adds unique nonempty email derived as lower(name)+"@example.test"; preserve IDs and names. Duplicate normalized names or any invalid input must leave schema, data and user_version exactly at version 0, not partially migrated. Success sets user_version=1; rollback on this authorized disposable fixture returns the original id/name schema and version 0 without losing those rows. Evaluate schema/migration and transaction trade-offs before implementation, add real SQLite tests for success, duplicate failure and rollback, and verify with the installed Node SQLite module. This breaking data-contract migration and rollback of the derived column are explicitly authorized only for this fixture. Do not touch a real database or install dependencies.

files.migrate.js: export function migrate(db){db.exec('ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email TEXT');for(const row of db.prepare('SELECT id,name FROM users').all())db.prepare('UPDATE users SET email=? WHERE id=?').run(row.name.toLowerCase()+'@example.test',row.id);db.exec('CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_unique ON users(email); PRAGMA user_version=1');}
files.migrate.test.js: import test from 'node:test';import assert from 'node:assert/strict';import {DatabaseSync} from 'node:sqlite';import {migrate} from './migrate.js';test('derives an email',()=>{const db=new DatabaseSync(':memory:');try{db.exec("CREATE TABLE users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,name TEXT NOT NULL);INSERT INTO users VALUES(1,'Alice')");migrate(db);assert.equal(db.prepare('SELECT email FROM users').get().email,'alice@example.test');}finally{db.close();}});
